Thanks again for the demo this morning — Mike and I appreciated the runtime/latency discussion. Quick recap and next asks from our side so we can move the procurement team: 

- Economic buyer: Mike Thompson (cc'd on this thread). He'll need a short one-pager on pricing + expected unit economics for our baseline workload.
- Legal/procurement: Sarah Li (legal) will require SOC 2 Type II evidence, DPAs, and confirmation on data retention/replication.

Team — forwarding Acme's asks (see Elena's note below). Quick summary and ask:

Summary of external asks:
- Confirm SOC 2 Type II and DPA (security will handle evidence).
- Confirm SLA target: 99.9% availability + financial credits.
- Pricing flexibility: customer requests 15-20% discount for 12-month commit and Net 45 payment terms.

My recommendation to stay competitive: offer 15% discount tied to a 12-month committed spend (minimum $150k ARR), agree to 99.9% SLA with a standard credit schedule, and keep Net 30 by default but allow Net 45 for procurement if legal signs off on DPAs and the exception request is approved.

Please review the attached procurement-exception-request (draft) and let me know:
1) Are you comfortable approving a 15% discount for this deal?
2) Can we agree to a 99.9% SLA (we may need a security exception for some logging/retention specifics; Vivek please advise)
3) Any other legal/finance constraints we should surface to Acme now?

Attachments: procurement-exception-request-20261201.pdf (draft)

I need a response by EOD tomorrow — Acme is planning a procurement review on Friday.

Marissa — reviewed Acme's request and your recommended commercial. My quick take:

- Discount: Approve up to 15% discount contingent on a 12-month committed spend (minimum $150k ARR). We should not go to 20% without escalation to sales management.
- Payment terms: Prefer to keep Net 30; Net 45 can be granted as a procurement exception if finance/legal approve the DPA and we have a signed SOW.
- SLA: 99.9% availability is acceptable, subject to security's confirmation on monitoring and incident response SLAs. If security needs additional logging/retention changes, those should be scoped as a documented exception.

Please move forward with these terms and get security/legal sign-off. Tag me if anything requires an exception above 15% or special SLA credits.

Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
